stories.title: Anthropic to allocate 5% of its shares to public‑benefit fund
stories.summary: Anthropic announced it will set aside 5 % of its outstanding shares in a wholly‑owned public‑benefit fund. The fund can make large donations to nonprofit organisations and direct distributions to address societal challenges such as AI’s impact on employment, and it will not be used for lobbying or political contributions. The company also said it may increase the fund’s stake by an additional 2 % for every 50 % rise in Anthropic’s valuation.
stories.why: It demonstrates a leading AI company committing equity to address public‑interest concerns and potential societal risks of AI.
stories.previousTitle: Anthropic says it’s committing 5% of its shares to a ‘public benefit fund’
stories.previousSummary: Anthropic announced on Oct. 18 that it will create a “public benefit fund” by committing 5% of its shares to a wholly‑owned entity within the company, with an option to add another 2% for every 50% rise in Anthropic’s value. The fund may be used for large donations to traditional nonprofits or direct distributions to specific populations, and the company notes it has already pledged $200 million to study AI’s impact on the job market.

stories.title: Austrian Airlines flight from Tel Aviv to Vienna diverts to Sofia after bomb threat
stories.summary: An Austrian Airlines Airbus A320 en route from Tel Aviv to Vienna was forced to make an emergency landing in Sofia, Bulgaria, after a bomb threat was reported. Bulgarian authorities escorted the aircraft with a MiG‑29 fighter jet and evacuated all passengers; no injuries were reported. The Bulgarian transport ministry said an investigation has been opened.
stories.why: The incident illustrates how airlines and air‑traffic authorities respond to potential security threats to protect passengers.

stories.title: US official says trade deal with India near completion
stories.summary: On Monday, Marco Rubio said the United States is very close to finalising a trade agreement with India. He noted that the progress of the negotiations is one factor the administration weighs when considering national‑security waivers related to Russian oil and gas sanctions. The remarks were reported by The Economic Times.
stories.why: Trade developments can affect currencies, business costs, market access and the external balance of the economies involved.
